_README: The largest box, in CSS pixels, that each picture ever paints into. Multiply
by dpr (and headroom) to get the pixels the file actually needs.
These are MEASURED, not guessed: the game was walked screen by screen at a
375px viewport and every and background-image had its rendered width
recorded as a fraction of the viewport, then scaled to 430 (an iPhone Pro Max
in portrait, the widest phone this targets). Re-measure with the sweep in
tools/measure_art_sizes.js after any layout change that resizes art.
Keys are path prefixes, matched longest-first, so a single file overrides its
directory. A picture with NO entry here is SKIPPED, not guessed at - run
`python tools/optimize_art.py --report-missing` to see what is unmeasured.
That is deliberate: skipping costs bytes, guessing low ships blurry art.
NOT LISTED ON PURPOSE: anything with a zoom state I could not reach in the
browser - card art (a card can be inspected full-size), patron portraits, and
the match table props. Those need measuring in their zoomed state first.
